title: PS5 Games on PC With No Emulator? How AnyPS5 Does It
description:
PS5 games on PC with no emulator: AnyPS5 is an open-source (GPL-2.0) tool that rewrites a PlayStation 5 game into a native Windows or Linux program, so the game runs as an ordinary process. So far, one game works. It's GitHub's top trending repository this week: 16,380 stars, 10,243 of them in the last 7 days.

How it works
• The PS5's CPU is an AMD Zen 2: x86-64, the same instruction set as a PC, so the game's code can run natively (a --to-intel option rewrites the few AMD-only instructions for Intel CPUs).
• What a PC lacks is Sony's system libraries (graphics, audio, controllers…). AnyPS5's relinker turns the game's executable into a Linux ELF or Windows PE program and links its calls to AnyPS5's own implementations of those libraries: 2,575 of the 3,038 functions it knows so far (85%).
• GPU shaders written for the PS5's AMD graphics are recompiled to SPIR-V and drawn through Vulkan. Its shader recompiler covers all 1,166 GPU instructions it has met.

Where it stands (its compatibility list, 9 October 2026)
• One tested game: Dreaming Sarah (2D platformer), in game and playable on Windows; Linux not yet tested.
• 60 FPS on a GTX 1050 Ti with an i5-7500; 36 FPS on Intel HD Graphics 620 with an i5-7200.

The catch
It's early: one game, on Windows. It includes no games, keys, firmware or Sony libraries, so you need your own legally obtained game files (check the law where you live). Get it only from its GitHub page: fake "PS5 emulator" downloads are a classic malware trap.
